I've seen article title's like this before, usually with an ominous agenda too.

Doom and gloom articles often overstate the seriousness of what's going to happen, but generally there's some truth to be found somewhere. Considering this article's author is writing for UX Magazine I had to dig pretty deep to find even a grain of something I find useful. That and, ironically enough, it looks like UX Magazine is pretty dead on the content front with an article every 6 months or so.

I love articles like this.

Symptom 1: Free templates are great until you want to go beyond a static site. Once you then have to dig into the spaghetti of divs and CSS, most companies will relent and find someone who can make them a site that is both good looking AND scalable and will wonder why they ever thought they could get away cheaply.

Symptom 2: Yeah, let's just stop innovating. If we listened to this author, design patterns would've never evolved to where they are now, let alone where we'll be in 5 years

Symptom 3: I've heard this one for ages, in both web design and animation. Here's a new program, it's going to do your job better than you. Problem is, they never do and the go back to symptom 1 of making a mess of code that a human eventually has to come in and fix. Until we have true AI, this will never change.

Symptom 4: Any company that uses Facebook as their main web site does not get my business because it means they don't take their business seriously. If they can't be bothered to register a domain and make an informative site (and sure, they can mirror the content on Facebook and use Twitter and all that too) makes me wonder if they couldn't be bothered to do other things, like get proper business licenses.

Symptom 5: I think people are starting to wake up to the fact that Apps that just mirror web content are mostly useless, unless they offer specific functionality that you can't get on the site itself. And really, typing web addresses is hard? I wonder how these same people text all day long.

Lots of words that seem impressive but we've heard them all before and we're still employed making websites that offer new ideas and deliver new designs.
